samples.summary: `TextEditor.siblingsOf` returns the body blocks even when editing header/footer, so Tab / Cmd+] / Cmd+[ on a header or footer list item becomes a silent no-op
samples.evidence: `siblingsOf` (text-editor.ts:2863-2869) does `if (!info) return this.doc.document.blocks;` — the *body* array. But `TextEditor` supports header/footer editing (`this.editContext`, `getActiveLayout()` at 4579, `this.doc.getContextBlocks()` used everywhere else, and `Doc.getBlock` searches `_document.header?.blocks` separately at document.ts:207). For a caret on a list item in the header, `forEachBlockInSelection` now calls `fn(cursorBlock, this.doc.document.blocks)`; `planSiblingGroup` then scans that body array for `selectedIds.has(block.id)` and never finds the header block, so it returns zero changes and `applyListLevelChanges` writes nothing. Before this change `handleTab`/`handleIndent` called `setBlockType(b.id, …)` directly and worked in any context. Note editor.ts's twin `siblingsOf` (editor.ts:1616) correctly uses `doc.getContextBlocks()` — the two implementations disagree.

samples.summary: Toolbar indent/outdent mutate descendant blocks that are never passed to `markDirty`, so the incremental layout cache repaints them at their old list indent
samples.evidence: `applyListLevelChanges` now rewrites `listLevel` on nested children that lie *outside* the selection, but the only `markDirty` calls come from `forEachBlockInSelection`, which visits selected blocks only (editor.ts:1698, 1707). `indent()`/`outdent()` then call `render()` without `invalidateLayout()`. In `computeLayout` a block that is not in `dirtyBlockIds` reuses cached lines (layout.ts:535-536), and the list indent is baked into the laid-out lines via `effectiveBlock.style.marginLeft = marginLeft + LIST_INDENT_PX * (listLevel + 1)` (layout.ts:493-501, 543). So an unselected child that just moved a level keeps its previous indentation on screen until some later full relayout. `text-editor.ts` avoids this by calling `invalidateLayout()`; `editor.ts` does not.

samples.summary: `siblingsOf` silently drops the change when the block's cell is not in `layout.blockParentMap` (e.g. a list item in a header/footer table cell)
samples.evidence: editor.ts:1612-1621 resolves the cell from `layout.blockParentMap` (the *body* layout; header/footer have their own `headerLayout`/`footerLayout`). If the map has no entry for a cell-internal block, `siblingsOf` falls back to `doc.getContextBlocks()`, which does not contain that block; `planSiblingGroup` then finds no selected id and the indent/outdent is a silent no-op rather than the old direct `setBlockType(block.id, …)`. The `cell?.blocks ?? [block]` fallback covers only the case where the map entry exists but the cell is gone.

samples.summary: Multi-block branch pairs context-relative indices with the body block array; in header/footer context the plan is built from (and applied to) the wrong blocks
samples.evidence: `startIdx`/`endIdx` come from `this.doc.getBlockIndex(...)`, which indexes `getContextBlocks()` (document.ts:272 → header/footer array in those contexts), but the new `const topLevel = this.doc.document.blocks;` (line 2836) is always the body. `fn(b, topLevel)` therefore hands out body blocks — and now also a body sibling array — for a header/footer selection, so a multi-block indent edits unrelated body blocks. The wrong-index read pre-dates this change, but the diff now also derives subtree/sibling structure from it.

finding.summary: `TextEditor.siblingsOf` returns the body blocks even when editing header/footer, so Tab / Cmd+] / Cmd+[ on a header or footer list item becomes a silent no-op
finding.evidence: `siblingsOf` (text-editor.ts:2863-2869) does `if (!info) return this.doc.document.blocks;` — the *body* array. But `TextEditor` supports header/footer editing (`this.editContext`, `getActiveLayout()` at 4579, `this.doc.getContextBlocks()` used everywhere else, and `Doc.getBlock` searches `_document.header?.blocks` separately at document.ts:207). For a caret on a list item in the header, `forEachBlockInSelection` now calls `fn(cursorBlock, this.doc.document.blocks)`; `planSiblingGroup` then scans that body array for `selectedIds.has(block.id)` and never finds the header block, so it returns zero changes and `applyListLevelChanges` writes nothing. Before this change `handleTab`/`handleIndent` called `setBlockType(b.id, …)` directly and worked in any context. Note editor.ts's twin `siblingsOf` (editor.ts:1616) correctly uses `doc.getContextBlocks()` — the two implementations disagree.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described. `TextEditor.siblingsOf` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2863-2869) returns `this.doc.document.blocks` (the body array) whenever the block is not inside a table cell, ignoring `this.editContext`. `forEachBlockInSelection`'s cursor fallback (2855-2856) pairs the caret block — which `Doc.getBlock` resolves from `_document.header?.blocks`/`footer?.blocks` (document.ts:203-215) — with that body array. `planListLevelChanges`/`planSiblingGroup` (model/list-level.ts:97-118, 64-67) only emit changes for ids found within the supplied siblings array, so a header/footer list item yields zero changes and `applyListLevelChanges` (text-editor.ts:2712-2723) writes nothing. The path is reachable: `case 'Tab'` (1120-1123) and `'['`/`']'` (1306-1315) dispatch to handleTab/handleIndent/handleOutdent with no editContext gate (unlike the explicit gates at 1114 and 4330), header/footer editing is fully supported (editContext at 183, setEditContext 403-406, getActiveLayout 4579-4581), and header list items are creatable via toggleList (2732-2748) / tryAutoConvert (2888-2903), which call setBlockType on the cursor block in any context. The sibling implementation in editor.ts:1612-1621 correctly uses `doc.getContextBlocks()`, confirming the divergence. Silent no-op of a feature on a normally reachable path = major correctness bug; no guard makes it unreachable.

finding.summary: Toolbar indent/outdent mutate descendant blocks that are never passed to `markDirty`, so the incremental layout cache repaints them at their old list indent
finding.evidence: `applyListLevelChanges` now rewrites `listLevel` on nested children that lie *outside* the selection, but the only `markDirty` calls come from `forEachBlockInSelection`, which visits selected blocks only (editor.ts:1698, 1707). `indent()`/`outdent()` then call `render()` without `invalidateLayout()`. In `computeLayout` a block that is not in `dirtyBlockIds` reuses cached lines (layout.ts:535-536), and the list indent is baked into the laid-out lines via `effectiveBlock.style.marginLeft = marginLeft + LIST_INDENT_PX * (listLevel + 1)` (layout.ts:493-501, 543). So an unselected child that just moved a level keeps its previous indentation on screen until some later full relayout. `text-editor.ts` avoids this by calling `invalidateLayout()`; `editor.ts` does not.

verdict.reason: The finding checks out exactly as described. `planListLevelChanges`/`planSiblingGroup` (model/list-level.ts:69-81 with subtreeOf at 26-42) rewrite `listLevel` on nested children that are not in `selectedIds`, while the only `markDirty` calls come from `forEachBlockInSelection` (editor.ts:1654, 1674, 1698, 1707), which visits/marks selected blocks only. Toolbar `indent()`/`outdent()` (editor.ts:3568-3598) call `applyListLevelChanges` then `render()` without `invalidateLayout()` — contrast `toggleList` at editor.ts:3561 and the text-editor equivalents at text-editor.ts:2760, 2776 which do invalidate. `render()` (editor.ts:2246) → `recomputeLayout()` (editor.ts:1523-1532) hands the partially populated `dirtyBlockIds` plus `layoutCache` to `computeLayout`, where `canUseCache` is satisfied because `dirtyBlockIds != null` (layout.ts:456-459), so a block missing from the dirty set reuses cached lines (layout.ts:535-536). The list indent is baked into those lines: `effectiveBlock.style.marginLeft = marginLeft + LIST_INDENT_PX * (listLevel + 1)` (layout.ts:493-502) feeding `lineStartX = marginLeft + textIndent` (layout.ts:666-674). No other listener or guard invalidates the cache on this path (only markDirty/invalidateLayout call sites exist, none covering these descendants). Result: unselected nested children render at their previous indent after a toolbar indent/outdent until an unrelated full relayout — real, reachable in normal use, in the correctness lane.
